text:
Maya Singh: Heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we've seen a sharp uptick in GPU pod Pending across eu-west1. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up backoffs and GCE returning 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: quota or rate limited'. Pods sit Pending for 12-18m. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
Arjun Patel: Yep saw it. Looks correlated with spot GPU throttling for the nvidia-a100-preempt pool. Cluster-autoscaler attempted new node groups but API throttled during parallel creates, CA went into exponential backoff.
Emily Chen: Can you paste the CA log snippet?
Maya Singh: Pasted below (trimmed):
```
I0318 02:12:07.123456 1 clusterstate.go:540] scale up: nodes needed 8
E0318 02:12:09.654321 1 scale_up.go:345] Failed to create NodeGroup "gpu-spot-eu-west1": googleapi: Error 429: Quota exceeded, rateLimitExceeded
W0318 02:20:15.000000 1 utils.go:210] scale-up rejected: backoff active for group gpu-spot-eu-west1
```
Devon R.: Ops-bot shows a spike of ephemeral instance create failures too: cluster-bot reported 60% create error rate 02:05-02:22.
cluster-bot: [automated] Notifying on-call and opening incident: #INC-7328 (create-rate-limited in eu-west1 spot pool).
Arjun Patel: Root causes look like: 1) cloud provider API rate limit from parallel node creation 2) underlying spot pool intermittently not offering capacity (eviction waves) 3) CA backoff preventing fallback to on-demand pool.
Li Zhao: We need an immediate mitigation to unblock Pending GPU pods. Two options: A) reduce CA parallelism and add a warm on-demand fallback node pool scaled to 2-4 nodes that can accept critical pods, or B) temporarily bypass CA and create a dedicated on-demand GPU pool with higher provisioning limits. Cost vs latency tradeoff.
Emily Chen: For immediate unblock I'd prefer option B (manual create) + change PodPriority to move critical inference pods to the fallback pool. We can label fallback nodes with `node.kubernetes.io/fallback-gpu=true` and update pod nodeSelector/tolerations.
Maya Singh: I'll try creating a small on-demand pool now with different machine type to avoid the same quota bucket (a2 rather than a100). Command I'll run: 
```
gcloud container node-pools create fallback-gpu-ondemand --cluster=prod-eu-west1 --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --num-nodes=2 --node-labels=fallback-gpu=true,preemptible=false --region=eu-west1
```
Arjun Patel: Also adjust CA flags to avoid backoff swallowing fallback behavior: set `--max-node-provision-time=15m` and `--scale-up-from-zero=true` and lower `--max-bulk-scaling` so the CA doesn't request 8 nodes in parallel. Consider `--max-bulk-scaling=2`.
Devon R.: Quick patch suggestion: add a PriorityClass `platform-critical` at high priority and patch the Deployment for model-serving to use it. That ensures CA / manual pool prioritization works.
Maya Singh: Created the manual pool and patched the priority + nodeSelector for the canary-serving pod. After a restart a subset scheduled within ~4m. Pending count dropped from 67 -> 11. :thumbsup:
Li Zhao: Follow-ups: 1) create a 2-node warm pool (ondemand) with autoscaling min=1 max=4 and taint `taint/redundant=true:NoSchedule` + a toleration on critical pods. 2) Add a CA scale-up policy route so when GPU spot groups fail, CA will attempt ondemand fallback group. 3) Engage cloud support on quota/rate limit spikes.
Emily Chen: Example toleration snippet for critical pods: 
```
- key: "taint/redundant"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
  tolerationSeconds: 600
```
Arjun Patel: For longer-term: implement staggered node-group creation (exponential jitter between group creates) and add a prewarm bot that keeps 1-2 nodes in standby in each region. Also run a postmortem on the eviction wave to identify if a GPU SKU is being hit disproportionately.
Maya Singh: Logged action items in the incident ticket: manual pool creation (done), warm pool PR (in progress), CA flag changes (in progress), cloud support case (opened). Will keep thread updated.
Devon R.: Thanks. Also consider adding CA metric alert on 'scale-up backoff duration > 10m' so we detect earlier. :eyes:
